kjv: took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows
mine: Taking one of the stones of the place, he put it at his head
note: Hebrew meraashotav means "at his head" (place by the head), not "pillows"; the partitive me-avne takes one stone, as v.18 ("the stone") confirms, while the KJV makes it several.
Hebrew sullam occurs only here; from salal (to heap up), it likely denotes a ramp or stairway like the stepped approach of a temple tower, rather than a rung ladder.
Hebrew nora means fearsome, awe-inspiring; "dreadful" once meant that but now means very bad.
